records.title: Out-of-scope route families are still mounted and bundled in production, behind one HTTP gate; deploy refuses LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=off but not UNATTRIBUTED=report
records.evidenceAtHead: Still mounted at HEAD: server/bootstrap/register-advanced-platform-routes.ts:159 (/api/ana-cortex-ft), :162 (/api/regulatory-digital-twin), :163 (/api/submission-twin), :196 (/api/snowglobe); register-inline-routes.ts:148 (/api/nano-banana); register-regulatory-routes.ts:427 (/api/pdf-tasks), which still spawns 'cer_tasks.py' (server/routes/pdf-task-routes.ts:149-150; `git ls-files | grep -c cer_tasks.py` = 0); register-ai-routes.ts:28 (/api/ana -> ana-features.ts, 5,533 LOC). /api/agent-swarm is gone. No registrar consults launch scope: `git grep launchScopeEnforced -- server/bootstrap server/startup server/index.ts` = 0 hits; mountAll (server/bootstrap/mount-routes.ts:60-84) mounts every entry. I re-ran the auditor's method at HEAD: grep of app.use/path: '/api…' in server/bootstrap + server/startup gives 357 distinct prefixes; launchScopeApiVerdict with NODE_ENV=production gives launch 63, never-gated 19, infrastructure 12, out-of-scope 93, unmapped 170. So 263 are refused, against 262 of 366 at audit. Config: readLaunchScopeMode (server/services/entitlements/launch-scope.ts:45-58) still honours LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=off in production; it now only logs an error once (:34-41, commit 471e5a4cd). readUnattributedApiMode (:77-97) still accepts 'report' in production with a warn. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:632-655 now refuses a task definition whose LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE is anything but absent or 'on', or comes from a secret. No preflight checks LAUNCH_SCOPE_API_UNATTRIBUTED (`grep UNATTRIBUTED .github/workflows terraform` = 0). Background job: externalIntelligenceSweep is still default ON (server/jobs/externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:13,35; started at server/index.ts:280) although /api/external-intelligence (reg-change) is out-of-scope. Defense-in-depth: the gate checks `pathname.startsWith('/api/')` case-sensitively (server/middleware/moduleEntitlementGate.ts:112), while Express 5.2.1 mounts are case-insensitive. A node -e repro with the same gate shape gave /api/regulatory-digital-twin/x -> 403 and /API/regulatory-digital-twin/x -> 200 'reached router'. In AWS this is masked by CloudFront's case-sensitive '/api/*' behaviour (terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:8-23); there is no such mask locally.
records.fixedBy: 471e5a4cd (deploy-aws.yml:632-655 preflight refuses LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE other than on; launch-scope.ts:34-41,49 logs production off as an error). fbff77602 / bcc457edb narrowed what counts as launch (see ARCH-02).
records.remaining: (1) Every refused family is still mounted, imported and bundled in every production process, so the release boundary is one middleware (moduleEntitlementGate) rather than what ships. A gate defect, such as the case-sensitive prefix check, exposes them. (2) The server still boots and serves everything with LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=off (only the AWS deploy preflight refuses it; a compose/Replit/Helm deploy would not). LAUNCH_SCOPE_API_UNATTRIBUTED=report reopens 170 unmapped prefixes with only a warn, and the preflight does not check it. (3) /api/pdf-tasks spawns a Python script that does not exist. (4) The external-intelligence sweep for an out-of-scope surface runs nightly by default. (5) No esbuild define or tree-shake of refused families.
records.severityRationale: Downgraded from P1. In the one pilot topology (AWS ECS, NODE_ENV=production), the HTTP gate defaults to on/enforce. The deploy preflight now refuses LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=off. CloudFront's case-sensitive path patterns keep /API/* off the ALB. A pilot user therefore cannot reach refused families through the supported path. What remains is defense-in-depth, a CSV boundary that does not match the bundle, and an unguarded UNATTRIBUTED=report switch. These must close before enterprise GA but do not block a founder-supported pilot.
records.humanTestingNote: On a local deployment started with `npm run dev`, NODE_ENV is not production, so LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE defaults to OFF (launch-scope.ts:48). The rail and Apps catalog then show surfaces outside the launch catalog, their APIs answer, and AnA offers hidden-app tools. Testers will exercise screens that production refuses and may file bugs against them. Workaround: set LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=on and LAUNCH_SCOPE_API_UNATTRIBUTED=enforce in the test environment's .env, or test on the AWS staging stack (ECS sets NODE_ENV=production). A 403 LAUNCH_SCOPE on a non-catalog screen is then expected behaviour, not a defect.
records.instructions:
1. Founder: answer arch.md open question 4 in writing. May out-of-scope families be unmounted in production (code kept in tree)? Does any customer or demo rely on LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=off or LAUNCH_SCOPE_API_UNATTRIBUTED=report? Record the answer in the commit message. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (Rule 0).
2. Config hardening, independent of step 1. In server/services/entitlements/launch-scope.ts, readLaunchScopeMode (:45-58): when NODE_ENV=production and raw==='off', throw unless env.LAUNCH_SCOPE_ACCEPT_OPEN === 'true'. With the flag, emit one structured error naming the accepted risk (the AI_GOVERNANCE_ACCEPT_PERMISSIVE shape in server/startup/ai-governance-posture.ts). Apply the same rule in readUnattributedApiMode (:77-97) for raw==='report'. The name must match ^[A-Z0-9_]+_ACCEPT_[A-Z0-9_]+$, so the existing ACCEPT_OVERRIDES preflight in .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml (~:599-613) refuses it automatically. Also add an explicit preflight block next to :632-655: LAUNCH_SCOPE_API_UNATTRIBUTED must be absent or exactly 'enforce', and must not come from secrets.
3. Add a mount-time launch-scope skip. In server/bootstrap/mount-routes.ts add `export function mountIfLaunchScoped(app, path, ...handlers)`. It computes `launchScopeApiVerdict(path, buildPrefixMap(), NEVER_GATED)` (server/services/entitlements/launch-scope-api.ts, api-prefix-map.ts). It does not mount when launchScopeEnforced() is true and the verdict is 'out-of-scope', or 'unmapped' with readUnattributedApiMode()==='enforce'. It logs one info line per skipped family. Make mountAll (:60-84) call it per entry. Replace the direct app.use calls for the refused families, starting with: register-advanced-platform-routes.ts:159,162,163,196; register-inline-routes.ts:148; register-regulatory-routes.ts:427; register-ai-routes.ts:28. Leave routers mounted at bare '/api' to the gate. Keep static imports, so the routes-reach-the-bundle test stays green. This is not a capability deletion: the routes are already 403 in production, and the gate (moduleEntitlementGate.ts:112-133) remains the replacement path.
4. Fail closed in /api/pdf-tasks: server/routes/pdf-task-routes.ts:149 spawns the non-existent cer_tasks.py. Return 501 with an honest message before spawning, or leave the route unmounted under step 3.
5. In server/jobs/externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:35, when launchScopeEnforced() is true and launchScopeApiVerdict('/api/external-intelligence', …) is 'out-of-scope', do not schedule unless ENABLE_EXTERNAL_INTELLIGENCE==='true' is set explicitly. Log the posture line, as the opt-in jobs do.
6. Optional second phase, after the founder answer: add an esbuild `define` for a launch-only build flag in scripts/build-server.mjs so guarded branches tree-shake. Prove it with the esbuild metafile no longer listing files from the auditor's exclusive-refused list (routes/c2c, api/cmc, services/regulatory, grdhe…).
7. Verify by failing first. (a) New test server/bootstrap/__tests__/launch-scope-unmounted.test.ts: with NODE_ENV=production, walk the Express stack after registerPostStartRoutes the way scripts/ci/launch-scope-route-inventory.ts does, and assert no layer is mounted at /api/regulatory-digital-twin, /api/snowglobe, /api/nano-banana or /api/pdf-tasks. Run it at HEAD and show it red, then green. (b) Unit test: readLaunchScopeMode({NODE_ENV:'production', LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE:'off'}) throws without LAUNCH_SCOPE_ACCEPT_OPEN. It must fail first, because HEAD returns 'off'. (c) Feed the deploy preflight a task-def JSON with LAUNCH_SCOPE_API_UNATTRIBUTED=report and show it exits 1.
records.acceptance: 1) With NODE_ENV=production and no overrides, the running registration (scripts/ci/launch-scope-route-inventory.ts --rows on a throwaway DB) lists zero routes with verdict out-of-scope, and unmapped routes only where an infrastructure entry explains them. The new launch-scope-unmounted test was red at HEAD and is green after. 2) readLaunchScopeMode and readUnattributedApiMode throw in production for off/report unless LAUNCH_SCOPE_ACCEPT_OPEN=true; unit tests shown red at HEAD first. 3) deploy-aws.yml preflight fails a task definition carrying LAUNCH_SCOPE_API_UNATTRIBUTED=report or LAUNCH_SCOPE_ACCEPT_OPEN, shown with a fixture. 4) POST /api/pdf-tasks no longer spawns python3 for a missing file (501 or unmounted). 5) With enforcement on, boot logs show the external-intelligence sweep not scheduled unless explicitly enabled. 6) npm run ci:launch-scope-api and ci:launch-scope stay green; no launch screen gets a 403.
records.dependencies: ARCH-02 (sub-path verdicts must be right before unmounting by verdict); ARCH-09 (normalise /api case in the gate: moduleEntitlementGate.ts:112); founder answer to arch.md open question 4.

records.title: Launch prefixes still inherit by longest prefix: /api/ana, /api/rim and /api/global-ri closed, but /api/submission-ops, /api/ectd (v4 router) and /api/corpus still carry out-of-scope endpoints as launch
records.evidenceAtHead: Closed. The 'training' shell surface was removed from LAUNCH_SHELL_SURFACES (shared/constants/launch-scope.ts:197-203, CPO decision 2026-10-08, commit bcc457edb). Its apiPrefixes ['/api/enablement','/api/ana'] (shared/constants/ui-surface-registry.ui-v2.ts:1333) no longer make /api/ana launch. A tsx probe of launchScopeApiVerdict at HEAD (NODE_ENV=production) gives 'out-of-scope' for /api/ana/intelligence-feed, /gap-analysis, /change-impact, /therapeutic-areas, /guidance/webhook and /submission-chat/stream. No client file calls /api/ana/* (git grep in client/src = 0), so no launch screen regresses. /api/rim and /api/global-ri are now out-of-scope: project-home, program-journey and dossier-map dropped those claims (commit fbff77602; comments at ui-surface-registry.ts:226,641 and ui-surface-registry.ui-v2.ts:129). Still open. modulesForPath is unchanged longest-prefix inheritance (server/services/entitlements/api-prefix-map.ts:67-79), and there is no per-route allowlist (no such symbol in server/shared/scripts/ci). Probe results: /api/submission-ops/x -> launch, claimed by vault, gateway-transmittals and tasks plus non-launch device-tasks, device-validation, device-submission and communication-center. server/routes/submission-ops.ts (3,651 LOC, 36 endpoints) includes /automation/run, /hotspots, /workload, /unified-work, /command-center, /digests and /policies. /api/ectd -> launch, and register-document-routes.ts:140 mounts the eCTD v4.0 router there (/v4/validate, /v4/forward-compat, /controlled-vocab), although the pilot is eCTD v3.2.2. /api/corpus/x -> launch via artifacts-center (corpus-routes.ts: POST /ingest, /extract, GET /benchmark). /api/study-design -> launch via protocol-dev, which is now intentionally in the Authoring app (shared/constants/launch-scope.ts LAUNCH_APPS 'authoring'). scripts/ci/check-launch-scope-api.ts only proves launch client paths are not refused. It has no reverse check that a launch prefix hosts only launch endpoints.
records.fixedBy: bcc457edb (training leaves the launch shell, so /api/ana is out-of-scope); fbff77602 (/api/rim and /api/global-ri claims removed from launch surfaces)
records.remaining: Shared launch prefixes still make every sub-path launch. /api/submission-ops automation/hotspots/workload/command-center/digests (device and communication-center features), the eCTD v4 router under /api/ectd, and /api/corpus ingest are served in production as launch. There is no per-route allowlist or exclusion mechanism, and no CI check that a launch prefix carries only launch endpoints.
records.severityRationale: Downgraded from P1. The headline exposure, all 68 /api/ana feature endpoints riding on a shell claim, is closed, as are /api/rim and /api/global-ri. The remaining porous endpoints are tenant-scoped, authenticated and few. They widen the validated surface beyond the catalog but do not create a security or integrity hole for an invited pilot org. This should be closed before enterprise GA validation.
records.instructions:
1. Inventory. On a throwaway DB, run `NODE_ENV=production DATABASE_URL=… npx tsx scripts/ci/launch-scope-route-inventory.ts --out /tmp/routes.json --rows`. List every route whose verdict is 'launch' and whose longest matching prefix also has a non-launch claimant. At HEAD this includes at least /api/submission-ops, /api/ectd, /api/corpus, /api/regulatory-programs (vault, tasks + device-pma), /api/task-management and /api/projects.
2. For each such route, decide launch or not from the client: is it named by a file a launch or shell surface reaches? The import walker already in scripts/ci/check-launch-scope-api.ts answers this. Expected non-launch at HEAD: /api/submission-ops/{automation,hotspots,workload,unified-work,command-center,digests,approval-bottlenecks}, /api/ectd/v4/*, and /api/corpus/{ingest,extract} unless an artifacts-center file calls them.
3. Add an exclusion layer in server/services/entitlements/launch-scope-api.ts: `export const LAUNCH_API_EXCLUSIONS: Readonly<Record<string,string>>` (path prefix -> written reason). In launchScopeApiVerdict, check it before returning 'launch', at a segment boundary with the same matcher as modulesForPath. A match returns 'out-of-scope'. Every entry needs a reason, like LAUNCH_PLATFORM_API. Do not change modulesForPath: the module-entitlement gate also uses it.
4. Extend scripts/ci/check-launch-scope-api.ts with a reverse check. For each prefix in the built prefix map whose claimants mix launch and non-launch surfaces, every exclusion entry must be a sub-path of that prefix. Every client file a non-launch surface reaches must not name a path under that prefix that is still 'launch', unless a launch surface's code also names it; otherwise fail and print the path. Add a --selftest case that builds a mixed prefix with an unexcluded non-launch-only sub-path and shows exit 1.
5. Tests in server/services/entitlements/__tests__/: launchScopeApiVerdict('/api/submission-ops/automation/run', buildPrefixMap(), NEVER_GATED) === 'out-of-scope', and the same for '/api/ectd/v4/validate'. Run at HEAD and show both red; they return 'launch' today. Assert '/api/submission-ops/packages' and '/api/ectd/…' paths used by ectd-compile stay 'launch'.
6. Run npm run ci:launch-scope-api, ci:launch-scope-api:selftest, ci:launch-scope and the new tests. Commit on concept2cure-v2. No route code is deleted, so the deletion rule does not apply. If a sub-router should instead be split out (e.g. submission-ops automation into its own router at /api/submission-automation), name the moved endpoints in the commit.
records.acceptance: 1) The new verdict tests for /api/submission-ops/automation/run and /api/ectd/v4/validate are red at HEAD and green after. 2) The ci:launch-scope-api selftest shows the reverse check failing on a constructed mixed prefix. 3) The production route inventory lists no route under a mixed launch prefix that only non-launch client code names. 4) Every launch screen's API calls are still 'launch' (ci:launch-scope-api green). 5) Every LAUNCH_API_EXCLUSIONS entry carries a reason.
records.dependencies: None blocking. Should land before ARCH-01 step 3, so mount-time skipping uses correct sub-path verdicts.

records.title: AnA executor (now 21,833 lines, 731 handlers) still exposes 618 'in-scope' tools including out-of-catalog engines; hidden-app tools are now refused at execution on every path, but runtime is still default-allow
records.evidenceAtHead: server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts is 21,833 lines (21,038 at audit), with 731 registerToolHandler( calls and 925 `await import(`. The inventory server/services/ana/ana-launch-scope.inventory.json now classifies 618 tools inScope and 173 hidden; at audit it was 590 and 189 (node count of both versions). Still inScope at HEAD: assess_biosimilar_cmc, design_vaccine_cmc, assess_pv_causality, run_monte_carlo_simulation, assess_cell_therapy_manufacturing, run_python_script, and 27 device/510k/IVD/UDI/PMA-named tools. Engines still reachable only through AnA (importers = AnaToolExecutor.ts plus its *Tools.ts wrappers): services/biosimilar 2,608, vaccine 1,835, rare-disease 1,865, digital-health 1,870 and dose-optimization 2,154 LOC. Runtime is still default-allow: anaCapabilityInLaunchScope returns true for any name not on the hidden list (server/services/ana/ana-launch-scope.ts:59-67, line 65 `if (!surfaces) return true;`). There is no production allowlist with rationale (no allowlist file in server/services/ana). Fixed part: preHandlerRefusal now refuses hidden-app tools with LAUNCH_SCOPE when enforced (AnaToolExecutor.ts:482-495; commit 4597bacd4). At 92ccdba1 preHandlerRefusal (line 371) had no launch-scope check. Every handler stored by registerToolHandler is the instrumented wrapper that calls preHandlerRefusal (:564-575), and getToolHandler (:632) returns that wrapper. So MCP's callAnaHandler (server/mcp/tools/runtime.ts:96-114) now passes the launch-scope check too, and its 7 bridged tools are all inScope. governed-toolset.ts:95 still withholds hidden tools from the model.
records.fixedBy: 4597bacd4 (AnaToolExecutor.ts:482-495: hidden-app tools refused at execution for chat, sub-agents and MCP alike)
records.remaining: The executor still keeps about 141k LOC of out-of-catalog engines live and bundled. It grew by about 800 lines, and the in-scope set grew by 28. There is no per-launch-app production allowlist with rationale and eval reference, and runtime is still default-allow for unclassified names. Only ana-launch-scope.test.ts enforces classification in CI. Knowledge tools from domains outside the catalog (biosimilar, vaccine, cell therapy, PV causality, Monte Carlo, device, run_python_script) remain in the intended use by classification, not by a founder decision. The executor has not been split into launch and non-launch registries.
records.severityRationale: Kept at P1. Pilot users will use AnA inside every launch app, and AnA can run about 600 tools, many in domains outside the catalog and outside any validation package. That is an intended-use and CSV-scope gap a GxP buyer's QA will raise before relying on the system. It also conflicts with CLAUDE.md RULE 2 (no capability outside the catalog; numbers from validated deterministic engines). It needs a founder decision before pilot users rely on AnA in production. It can drop to P2 if the founder signs off the knowledge-tool set as intended use and documents it.
records.humanTestingNote: Not a launch-journey blocker. Exploratory testers who ask AnA about biosimilar or vaccine CMC, PV causality, Monte Carlo simulation or device topics will see AnA run tools from outside the launch catalog. Even on an enforced (production-mode) deployment these run because they are classified in-scope. On a local `npm run dev` stack (scope off) hidden-app tools run too. Record such outputs as scope observations for the founder decision, not as defects of the launch apps. Set LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=on locally to see the production tool set.
records.instructions:
1. Founder (arch.md open questions 1 and 2): decide which AnA tools are validated launch intended use, per launch app. Decide whether the knowledge tools from domains outside the catalog and run_python_script (see ARCH-07) are in scope. Record the decision in the commit and in a reviewed decision record.
2. Add server/services/ana/ana-production-allowlist.json in the form `{ "<tool>": { "app": "<LAUNCH_APPS id>", "rationale": "…", "evalRef": "…" } }`. Seed it only with tools the founder approved; the 7 MCP-bridged tools (server/mcp/tools/{intelligence,reference,validation}.ts) must be on it.
3. Default-deny at runtime. In server/services/ana/ana-launch-scope.ts add `anaToolOnProductionAllowlist(name)`. In AnaToolExecutor.ts preHandlerRefusal (:482-495), when launchScopeEnforced() is true and the tool is not on the allowlist, return the LAUNCH_SCOPE refusal; keep the existing hidden-app check. Every handler is wrapped by registerToolHandler (:564-575), so this covers the chat stream, sub-agents and MCP callAnaHandler (server/mcp/tools/runtime.ts:96-114) at once. Also filter governed-toolset.ts:95 with the allowlist, so unlisted tools are never offered to the model. Platform commands (inventory.commands) get the same treatment where AnaToolExecutor.ts:20140 checks them.
4. Change anaCapabilityInLaunchScope (ana-launch-scope.ts:65) so an unclassified name returns false when an explicit production flag is passed. Keep the classification test in ana-launch-scope.test.ts.
5. Split the executor so out-of-scope engines are not loaded by default. Move handlers into per-domain modules of at most 2,000 lines under server/services/ana/tools/ (e.g. tools/launch/*.ts and tools/extended/*.ts), each exporting `register(registerToolHandler)`. AnaToolExecutor.ts imports the launch index statically. It imports the extended index only when launch scope is off or the tool is allowlisted; static imports in the extended index keep the bundle check (scripts/ci/check-server-bundle-prod-imports.mjs) green. Verify with the esbuild metafile that services/{biosimilar,vaccine,rare-disease,digital-health,dose-optimization} are absent from a launch-only build, if founder step 1 removes them.
6. Verify by failing first. (a) New test server/services/ana/__tests__/ana-production-allowlist.test.ts: register a handler 'zz_unclassified_tool' via registerToolHandler, set NODE_ENV=production, call getToolHandler('zz_unclassified_tool') and assert a LAUNCH_SCOPE refusal. It is red at HEAD because ana-launch-scope.ts:65 allows it. (b) Assert every MCP-bridged tool is allowlisted. (c) Assert every allowlist entry has a non-empty rationale and an app in LAUNCH_APPS. Commit on concept2cure-v2. Removing tools from production is a product decision, so name the founder decision in the commit.
records.acceptance: 1) The allowlist JSON exists, and every entry has app, rationale and evalRef. 2) With NODE_ENV=production, a tool not on the allowlist is refused with LAUNCH_SCOPE via chat, sub-agent and MCP paths; the test is red at HEAD and green after. 3) governed-toolset offers only allowlisted tools in production (count asserted). 4) Executor files are each at most 2,000 lines (scripted line-count check in CI). 5) If the founder removes out-of-catalog domains, the esbuild metafile of the production build no longer contains server/services/{biosimilar,vaccine,rare-disease,digital-health,dose-optimization}. 6) ana-launch-scope.test.ts and the MCP tests stay green.
records.dependencies: Founder decision (arch.md open questions 1–2); ARCH-07 (run_python_script and Python runtime); ARCH-01 for the launch-only build define.

records.title: Default-on schedulers now run once per window across tasks via a Postgres lease and claim table; three opt-in writers stay unlocked and the orphaned ECS worker service is still declared
records.evidenceAtHead: server/db/scheduledOnce.ts (absent at 92ccdba1) adds runScheduledOnce: a session-level pg_try_advisory_lock(20260924, hashtext(job)) on a dedicated pooled connection (:73-93). It also adds runScheduledOncePerWindow, a durable claim row in scheduled_job_claims under the lease (:146-209). The table comes from migrations/20261001d_scheduled_job_claims.sql: public, organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL, IF NOT EXISTS, in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:3022. Wired callers: retentionCron.ts:409, externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:50, auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:612, chainIntegrityMonitor.ts:445, sentinel/scheduler.ts:149, digest-heartbeat.ts:179, memory-consolidation-job.ts:501, scheduleOfEventsSweep.ts:101 and citation-run-pruner.ts:146. taskDueSweep uses a guarded compare-and-set UPDATE on metadata markers (taskDueSweep.ts:87-106). The submission-chat sweep is an idempotent expiry UPDATE. securityHealthScheduler is a read-only self-test. `vitest run server/jobs/__tests__/nightly-sweeps-once-per-window.test.ts` passes 3/3. No CI gate requires a new scheduler to take the lease (no script in scripts/ci or package.json). Topology: api_desired_count = 2 is unchanged (terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:48-51; terraform.tfvars.example:46). The worker ECS service, task definition and ECR repo are still declared (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:24,281-310,366-395; terraform/stack/main.tf:31,402). The service runs from an empty 'worker' ECR repository, and worker_desired_count still defaults to 1 in terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:53-56; only the .tfvars example sets 0 (:47-50). deploy-aws.yml:61-64 keeps the TODO(infra) to remove it.
records.fixedBy: 03dbeaf51 (server/db/scheduledOnce.ts runScheduledOnce), 4b1583a2c (runScheduledOncePerWindow + migrations/20261001d_scheduled_job_claims.sql; retention, external-intelligence, audit-chain sweeps wired), f0533ac96 (chainIntegrityMonitor.ts:445 once per window)
records.remaining: (1) Three opt-in writers run once per process when enabled: drift sentinel, corpus ingestion and regulatory horizon scan. (2) No CI gate stops a new cron.schedule/setInterval job from skipping the lease. (3) The orphaned worker ECS service and ECR repo are still in Terraform, with production variable default worker_desired_count = 1.
records.severityRationale: Downgraded from P1. Every default-on job that writes, notifies or deletes, including the retention hard-DELETE from vault.documents, now runs once per window across both API tasks. The remaining unlocked jobs are off by default and outside the pilot's launch journeys. The orphaned worker cannot run (empty image repository), so it adds no third scheduler copy. What is left is regression prevention and infra hygiene before GA.
records.instructions:
1. Wrap the three remaining writers. server/jobs/driftSentinelSweep.ts:75: replace the direct `runDriftSentinelSweep()` call with `runScheduledOncePerWindow('drift-sentinel-sweep', windowKeyOf(intervalMs), () => runDriftSentinelSweep())`. server/jobs/corpusIngestionSweep.ts:164: `runScheduledOncePerWindow('corpus-ingestion-sweep', windowKeyOf(24*60*60*1000), () => runCorpusIngestionSweep())`. server/jobs/regulatoryHorizonScan.ts:154: `runScheduledOncePerWindow('regulatory-horizon-scan', windowKeyOf(24*60*60*1000), () => runRegulatoryHorizonScan())`. Import from '../db/scheduledOnce'. Use a one-day window for the weekly crons, because epoch-aligned 7-day windows start on Thursday.
2. Tests that fail first. Extend server/jobs/__tests__/nightly-sweeps-once-per-window.test.ts, or add a sibling, with the three jobs: mock runScheduledOncePerWindow to answer already_ran_this_window and assert the job-body spy is not called.
